A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same L²M research. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial rewriting and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original mutual-information measurements on PG19 and Wikipedia, Gaussian modeling experiments, and GPT2/Mamba evaluations on PG19, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical measurements and reports additional model/length evaluations, including the state-size-ratio analysis and 8192-token PG19 experiments.

M1.justification: The direct and vCLUB estimators, n-gram bias corrections, Gaussian construction, MLP input/output adaptations and training objectives remain unchanged. Revised theoretical definitions and expanded experimental configurations do not introduce a new algorithm or architecture.

E1.justification: Both versions use PG19, Wikipedia and the same synthetic Gaussian families for mutual-information analysis and autoregressive modeling. Expanded sequence-length sweeps change experimental settings within this retained coverage, without adding a dataset, language or distinct task.

E2.justification: Comparator membership changes in specific experiments: LLaMA 3.1 70B disappears from the density-estimator comparison in v1 Figure A.2, while GPT2-large joins the PG19 comparisons in v2 Figures 4 and G.9. The principal architecture families and direct/vCLUB comparison remain.

E3.justification: v2 adds 8192-token PG19 evaluations and expands the Gaussian Mamba sweep to lengths 64–16384 and sizes 50M–1.4B. The reported PG19 batch changes from 32768 to 16384 tokens, and the approximate five-epoch iteration count changes from 235000 to 450000, although both versions also state 500000 total steps. These are substantial reported setting changes, not evidence of same-setting performance improvements.

E4.justification: New Figure 3(c) tests whether Gaussian-model KL error collapses onto a common curve when plotted against mutual information divided by history-state size, providing a substantial direct analysis of the central prediction. Existing partition-ratio and bias-correction analyses remain, while the LLaMA 70B estimator-sensitivity evidence is removed.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence levels or significance tests. The existing mutual-information bias corrections, fitting procedures and associated plotting conventions remain; additional result curves do not establish a changed uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds the state-size-ratio collapse, 8192-token PG19 curves and additional model results, and revises the 4096-token comparisons under changed reported settings. Figure B.1 newly reports DeepSeek fitted exponents of 0.57 and 0.59. LLaMA 70B results and v1 Table F.1's average PG19 NLL scores disappear. The original LLaMA 405B scaling fits are retained.

T1.justification: Section 5 replaces exact MI matching by a model series with maximum-expressible-MI inequalities and separately formalizes single-model and model-series capability. Appendix B.VIII adds a conditional-MI decomposition. The proof routes already existed, but v2 corrects the chain-rule step in v1 Equation D.31 through Equation E.33. The Hilberg and compression derivations in v1 Appendices A.I–A.II are removed.

C1.justification: The central scaling-law and history-state necessity claims remain. The introduction and conclusion replace v1's claim that state size must scale 'faster' with a necessary lower bound, aligning the headline claim with the already permitted equal-rate scaling. The abstract also explicitly extends the prospective scope beyond natural language.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new collapse as dependence on the MI/state-size ratio and extrapolates memory requirements to million-token sequences. New discussion addresses transformer memory over-provisioning, diffusion models and other sequence domains; limitations explicitly identify the unresolved link to downstream performance. Conversely, the English-only caveat and explanations of DeepSeek/LLaMA estimator differences are removed.

D1.justification: New Tables F.1–F.2 disclose layer counts, hidden sizes and tested lengths, and v2 states that conditional-NLL curves are smoothed. Reported GPU capacity changes from 94GB to 96GB, and LLaMA 70B deployment details disappear. Most optimizer, precision, library and code-access information was already present.

R1.justification: v2 adds targeted positioning against universal prediction and variable-order Markov modeling, connects bipartite MI to predictive information, and expands discussion of InfoNCE and other estimators. Earlier detailed Hilberg/compression comparisons are reduced. Most of the existing related-work framework remains.

P1.justification: The abstract and substantial portions of the introduction, scaling-law explanation, theory, experiments and conclusion are rewritten. v2 adds a separate Discussion and notation appendix, reorganizes experimental details, and moves two-point estimation material into the appendices.

P2.justification: The main text switches from two columns to one, Figures 1–2 are redesigned, and several existing plots move to appendices. v2 adds the ratio-collapse panel and configuration tables, reorganizes PG19 plots into matched-size comparisons, boxes the L²M conditions, and removes the average-NLL table.

improvement.justification: v2 improves precision through the revised capability definitions and corrected chain-rule step, and strengthens empirical support with the state-size-ratio analysis and longer PG19 evaluations. Configuration tables and clearer downstream-performance limitations also help readers assess the work. These gains are partly offset by removing estimator-sensitivity evidence and aggregate NLL scores, while the new million-token implications remain extrapolations. The net quality improvement is useful but limited.
